page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The CPU includes 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2032.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1912.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4216.75 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4231.0. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score is poor at 978.31, and read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks is weak at 25.92 GB/sec, though write bandwidth for large blocks reaches an average of 27.34 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in workloads like cryptography and basic vector operations.

The c7i-flex.xlarge is designed as a cost-efficient alternative within the compute-optimized category, trading off peak multi-core and memory performance for a lower resource cost profile. It is best suited for workloads that require moderate single-threaded compute power but have low memory footprint and network demands, such as light web serving (achieving an average static web serving throughput of 7.82 GB/sec), basic text processing, and entry-level single-threaded batch processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
